decision.window_up: Charter within the next 1–2 weeks (rate trending up)
decision.window_down: You can wait 2–4 weeks (rate trending down)
decision.window_flat: Rate is stable; charter on your normal schedule
decision.summary: For {commodity} into {destination}, the route freight rate is forecast to {direction} to about ${forecast:.2f}/unit. {risk_text} {window}. {note}
decision.idle_high: Estimated turnaround at discharge is ~{days} days, above the 4-day comfort band. Pre-book a laycan window with buffer, and line up a backhaul or repositioning cargo so the vessel isn't idle waiting at anchorage.
decision.idle_down: Rates are trending down — consider a short ballast reposition toward a firmer nearby load port, or hold the vessel on a 1–2 week extendable option.
decision.idle_slow: Estimated turnaround at discharge is ~{days} days. Coordinate berth prioritization in advance to avoid anchorage queueing and idle days.
decision.idle_ok: Turnaround and market direction look manageable; no special idle-time mitigation needed.
decision.contract_high: Market volatility is high — a Contract of Affreightment (COA){duration} locking in today's terms across multiple voyages hedges against future rate spikes better than repeated spot fixtures.
decision.contract_up: Rates are trending up — securing a short/mid-term COA{duration} now, rather than re-entering the spot market voyage-by-voyage, locks in the current rate before further increases.
decision.contract_down: Rates are trending down — a short spot or index-linked fixture is preferable to a long COA right now; revisit COA coverage once rates stabilise.
decision.contract_flat: Rates look stable — a mid-term COA{duration} can still reduce chartering overhead versus repeated single spot voyages.
decision.voyages: At {cargo:,.0f}t per lift, the {total:,.0f}t program implies roughly {voyages} voyages.
decision.congestion_none: No elevated port-congestion risk flagged for this route.
decision.compare_note: The freight-rate forecast reflects global dry-bulk market conditions and does not vary by loading port. Origins are ranked by vessel feasibility at both the load and discharge ports, estimated transit time, and load-port congestion — the factors that actually differ by origin for a fixed destination and commodity.
decision.idle_note: Ranked by a composite score combining predicted freight-rate earnings and ballast/idle time to the next load port — use alongside the idle-scenario-management guidance on a specific forecast for shipment-level planning.
decision.idle_reposition_note: Reposition to {origin} to load {commodity} back toward {current_port}.
decision.vessel_not_recognized: Requested vessel type '{vessel}' is not a recognized vessel class.
decision.vessel_requested_rejected: The requested {vessel} is not feasible ({reason}); {selected} is recommended instead. {note}
decision.vessel_draft_check: draft {draft:.1f} m against a port limit of {limit:.1f} m
decision.vessel_loa_check: LOA {loa:.0f} m against a port limit of {limit:.0f} m
decision.port_data_warning: Infrastructure data for one or both ports is limited or estimated; treat draft, LOA, and beam constraints as indicative only.
decision.vessel_capacity_normal: {vessel} is the smallest vessel class whose dataset-derived typical DWT can carry approximately {cargo:,.0f} tonnes.
decision.vessel_capacity_over: The cargo quantity of approximately {cargo:,.0f} tonnes exceeds the typical dataset-derived capacity of the largest vessel class ({vessel}); {vessel} is shown as the closest available reference.
decision.vessel_fit_ok: Its typical draft of {draft:.1f} m is within the destination port depth of {port_depth:.1f} m.
decision.vessel_fit_unknown: Port depth or draft data is not fully available for this route, so this feasibility check is approximate.
decision.vessel_fit_fail_alt: {vessel}'s typical draft of {draft:.1f} m exceeds the {port_label} depth of {port_depth:.1f} m, so {alt} is recommended instead as the largest class that fits both ports.
decision.vessel_fit_fail_none: {vessel}'s typical draft of {draft:.1f} m exceeds the {port_label} depth of {port_depth:.1f} m, and no dataset vessel class fits both ports for this cargo; treat this recommendation as indicative only.
decision.timing_up: Freight rates are trending up, so consider chartering sooner rather than later.
decision.timing_down: Freight rates are trending down, so there may be room to wait before chartering.
decision.draft_exceeds_max: A typical draft of {draft:.1f} m exceeds the maximum permitted draft of {max_draft:.1f} m.
decision.delay_note: An additional {delay:g} day(s) of expected delay flagged on this request has been folded into the turnaround estimate above.
decision.transit_provided: Using the supplied distance of {distance_km:,.0f} km, estimated sea transit from {origin} to {destination} is about {days} days at a typical {speed:.1f}-knot laden bulk-carrier service speed.
decision.transit_table: Estimated sea transit from {origin} to {destination} is about {days} days, based on an indicative route-distance table (no distance was supplied on the request).
decision.transit_unavailable: No distance was supplied, and this origin-destination pair is not in the indicative route-distance table, so a transit-time estimate is not available.
decision.stowage_light: At {factor:.2f} m3/t, this cargo is relatively light/bulky for its weight (typical dry-bulk cargoes run roughly 0.4-1.6 m3/t) — cubic capacity, not deadweight, may end up being the binding constraint on vessel choice; confirm against the specific vessel class grain/bale capacity.
decision.stowage_dense: At {factor:.2f} m3/t, this cargo is relatively dense for its weight (typical dry-bulk cargoes run roughly 0.4-1.6 m3/t) — deadweight is very likely the binding constraint, consistent with the DWT-based vessel check above.
decision.stowage_typical: At {factor:.2f} m3/t, the implied stowage factor is within the typical dry-bulk range (roughly 0.4-1.6 m3/t); deadweight is the expected binding constraint, consistent with the vessel check above.
decision.mode_charter: Shipment mode is set to Charter — the figures above are framed as a chartering/COA decision (vessel hire under a charter party) rather than a one-off freight booking; the per-ton rate remains the reference point since this pipeline does not model daily hire-rate equivalents.
decision.mode_spot: Shipment mode is set to Bulk Carrier (spot voyage) — the figures above are framed as a single voyage-charter booking at the quoted per-ton rate.
rejection.cargo: Cargo of {cargo:,.0f} t exceeds {vessel}'s typical DWT capacity of {dwt:,.0f} t.
rejection.loa: {port} LOA limit: {vessel} LOA ({value:.0f} m) exceeds the port maximum ({limit:.0f} m).
rejection.beam: {port} beam limit: {vessel} beam ({value:.1f} m) exceeds the port maximum ({limit:.1f} m).
rejection.draft: {port} draft limit: {vessel} draft ({value:.1f} m) exceeds the port usable depth ({limit:.1f} m).
rejection.unknown: Vessel feasibility cannot be confirmed for {vessel} because infrastructure data is unavailable for {port}.
rejection.generic: {vessel} is not feasible for the stated cargo and port constraints.
forecast.risk_reliability: heuristic (rule-based, not a trained classifier) — see risk_factors
compare.no_port_data: No port infrastructure data available for this origin.
compare.ais_source: AISStream live AIS feed (this origin only, last 24h)
coa.no_fit_ports: Does not fit the port constraints at one or both ends.
coa.capacity_too_small: {cls}'s effective capacity ({cap:,.0f} t) is smaller than the requested cargo/voyage of {requested_lift:,.0f} t.
coa.schedule_fits: Fits inside the requested contract window.
coa.schedule_short: Requires ~{required_schedule_days:.0f} days vs {contract_days:.0f} available; contract window is too short for this vessel/voyage plan.
coa.none_carry_lift: No vessel class can carry the requested cargo/voyage at both origin and destination ports.
coa.none_feasible_program: No vessel class is feasible at both origin and destination ports for the COA program.
coa.note_selected: Selected from schedule-feasible vessel strategies. Savings are shown only when a current spot benchmark is supplied.
coa.note_no_schedule: No vessel strategy fits the full COA within the requested contract window; increase duration, reduce program tonnage, or split the program.
coa.note_no_spot: No current spot benchmark supplied; ranking is operational and no monetary savings are claimed.
coa.method_fixed_lift: Cargo/voyage was supplied, so it is used as a fixed lift size: only vessel classes able to carry it are considered, and voyage count is total_program_tons ÷ that lift size. Uses direct observed-route forecasts when available or an AIS-enhanced market proxy calibrated to a user-supplied spot benchmark otherwise, and adds a transparent risk buffer. It is not a broker/charter quote.
errors.no_route_forecast: No synthetic route-freight forecast is available for {origin} -> {destination}{commodity_part}. This lane is not covered by the route-freight dataset, or its held-out evaluation did not beat the naive-persistence baseline.
coa.method_enumerate: Enumerates both-port-feasible vessel classes, computes COA voyage count from dataset-derived typical DWT, uses direct observed-route forecasts when available or an AIS-enhanced market proxy calibrated to a user-supplied spot benchmark otherwise, and adds a transparent risk buffer. It is not a broker/charter quote.
